text.p: Wilson HTM Ltd was recommending Pan Australian Resources NL as a buy following the junior explorer's release of early exploration results in its West Australian and Queensland tenements.

"The significance of the (exploration) work in the Yilgarn extension project lies in the correlation with the prolific Eastern goldfields to the north of the Pan Aust tenements," Wilson's resources research, Phil Hutchings said in a report.
He said additional work in the company's Cameron River project near Cloncurry in north Queensland had also increased the size of four targets and delineated three new copper anomalies.
Hutchings said interpretation by Pan Australia of a detailed aeromagnetic survey in the Yilgarn extension, south of Norseman in Western Australia, produced 41 priority targets.
Results of geochemical exploration confirmed the area had anomalous gold in the soil cover.

"These early results confirm the area is underlain by Archaean greenstone lithologies and also confirm there is anomalous gold associated with the structural targets within this new unexplored greenstone belt," Hutchings said.

"Based on the size of the greenstone areas and evident continuity of the structures with the main Norseman-Kambalda-Kalgoorlie belt to the north, we believe the area has potential to host one or more gold deposits," Hutchings said.
These deposits could be similar to the prolific gold-producing zone to the north, Hutchings said.
In Queensland, the company's Cameron River project comprised a 100 percent-held exploration permit and a permit where Pan Australian was earning a controlling interest from Dominion Mining, he said.

Hutchings said the Cameron River project was within the protozoic Mt Isa inlier area with the target being a Ernest Henry-style deposit on the western flank. A 10,000-metre drilling programme had now been completed, he said.
"This work has increased the size of four targets and delineated three new copper anomalies," Hutchings said.
